scan.notes: Static collectors ran fully. Network collector ran against the authorized loopback target only. IOC data age: 3 days.

summary.grade_reason: One or more high-confidence Critical findings: CHS finding sec-net-001 (networked path reachable without auth) and node-mal-001 (known-malicious node present).

findings.title: ComfyUI reachable with no authenticating layer
findings.evidence: HTTP 200 with no auth challenge; no reverse-proxy auth signature observed.
findings.description: The instance answers unauthenticated API requests. ComfyUI core has no authentication, so any reachable client can submit workflows via POST /prompt.
findings.impact: Any network-reachable client can execute an arbitrary node graph as the ComfyUI process user.

remediation.summary: Bind to loopback or a private interface and require an authenticating TLS proxy.
remediation.action: Remove non-loopback --listen; place nginx/Caddy/Cloudflare Access in front with TLS and auth.

findings.title: Bind address is non-loopback
findings.description: The launch configuration binds all interfaces via --listen 0.0.0.0.
findings.impact: Exposes every unauthenticated endpoint to the network.

remediation.summary: Bind 127.0.0.1 and reach the instance through an authenticating proxy.

findings.title: Known-malicious custom node present
findings.evidence: Directory name and file hashes match the Upscaler-4K / Akira Stealer IOC set; payload staged under scripts/.
findings.description: This node matches a known info-stealer campaign that hid its payload in a scripts/ subfolder and persisted a hidden executable.
findings.impact: Credential and wallet theft, persistence, and outbound exfiltration when the node loads.

remediation.summary: Move the node out of custom_nodes to a quarantine location; do not delete; investigate persistence artifacts.
remediation.action: Quarantine the directory, then check for AppData/Roaming/DisplayUpdater.exe and related persistence.
remediation.rollback: Restore from quarantine only after confirming it is a false positive.

findings.title: Core version predates the July 2026 traversal and XSS fixes
findings.evidence: Installed core resolves below the patched build for CVE-2026-56670/56672/56673 and GHSA-pj59-g5vv-74q4.
findings.description: Path traversal in LoadImage and model-preview, and stored XSS in /view and /userdata, were fixed in the July 2026 release.
findings.impact: Unauthenticated file-existence probing, limited file read, and token-stealing XSS when networked.

remediation.summary: Upgrade core to the patched release.
remediation.action: Update ComfyUI core; re-run smoke-test workflows before returning to service.
remediation.rollback: Pin the prior commit if a workflow regresses.

findings.title: ComfyUI-Manager below 3.38 (config-exposure RCE)
findings.evidence: Manager 3.29.0 stores config under user/default/, reachable through the core web API (CVE-2025-67303).
findings.description: An unauthenticated attacker can read and rewrite Manager config to downgrade the security level and reach RCE.
findings.impact: Remote code execution on a networked instance.

remediation.summary: Upgrade Manager to 3.38+ and core to 0.3.76+, then run the userdata migration.
remediation.action: Update Manager and core; follow the userdata security migration guide.
remediation.rollback: N/A; keep a backup of user/ before migrating.

findings.title: Custom node makes an exfiltration-shaped network call
findings.evidence: requests.post('https://discord.com/api/webhooks/REDACTED', ...) with a payload built from local file reads
findings.description: A hardcoded Discord webhook receives data assembled from local reads. This matches the LLMVISION exfiltration pattern, though it can also be a benign notification feature.
findings.impact: Potential exfiltration of local data when the node runs.

remediation.summary: Review the node's intent; remove or gate the outbound call, and restrict egress at the host.
remediation.action: Inspect post_result; confirm what is sent and to whom.

findings.title: Custom node installs a package at runtime
findings.description: Runtime pip install runs at ComfyUI startup. This is banned by the Comfy Registry standards and was part of the Upscaler-4K chain.
findings.impact: Uncontrolled dependency fetch and code execution at startup.

remediation.summary: Declare the dependency in requirements.txt and remove the runtime install.
remediation.action: Move 'somepkg' to requirements.txt; delete the subprocess call.

findings.title: Checkpoint contains a dangerous pickle import
findings.evidence: Static opcode scan found a GLOBAL/REDUCE referencing 'posix.system' (not on the safe allowlist). File not deserialized.
findings.description: The checkpoint's pickle stream references a shell-exec callable, which would run on load.
findings.impact: Code execution when the checkpoint is loaded.

remediation.summary: Quarantine the file; do not load it; prefer a safetensors equivalent from a trusted source.
remediation.action: Move the file to quarantine and record its source.
remediation.rollback: Restore only if confirmed safe by an independent tool.

findings.title: ComfyUI runs as root in the container
findings.evidence: Container image has no USER directive; process runs as uid 0.
findings.description: Running as root maximizes the blast radius of any node-level code execution.
findings.impact: A node RCE becomes host-root-equivalent inside the container.

remediation.summary: Add a non-root USER with a fixed UID/GID.
remediation.action: Add a comfy user to the Dockerfile and set USER; align bind-mount ownership.

findings.title: Manager install flags enabled on a networked instance
findings.description: A weak security level permits high-risk install operations regardless of network exposure.
findings.impact: Widens the Manager RCE surface on an exposed instance.

remediation.summary: Set security_level to strong and disable the install flags unless actively needed.

findings.title: Cloud credential in the process environment
findings.evidence: A secret-shaped value is present in the environment (value redacted).
findings.description: Any in-process custom node can read the whole environment. A secret placed here is readable by all nodes, not just the one that needs it.
findings.impact: A single malicious or compromised node can exfiltrate the credential.

remediation.summary: Move the secret to a mounted file with restrictive permissions or a secrets manager; rotate it.
remediation.action: Relocate the secret; the credential owner rotates it.

findings.title: Unpinned dependency in a custom node
findings.description: An unpinned dependency can pull in a future compromised release.
findings.impact: Supply-chain exposure at the next install or update.

remediation.summary: Pin the dependency to a known-good version with a hash.
remediation.action: Set somepkg==<version> and add a hash where feasible.
